entertainment.title: Christopher Abbott Reveals How His ‘You Can See Everything’ Moment Came to Be
entertainment.summary: The actor appears alongside Amanda Seyfried in Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's hit doc.
entertainment.body:
The You Can See Everything secrets are finally coming out , and Christopher Abbott is opening up about his surprise role in Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim ‘s hit documentary.

The actor — currently garnering acclaim for East of Eden and booked as Professor X in Marvel’s upcoming X-Men reboot — appears alongside Amanda Seyfried in several parts of the film, portraying Elizabeth Holmes’ husband Billy Evans while Seyfried plays Holmes . The pair are brought in to recreate the filmmakers’ interactions with the couple, both in moments that occurred off camera and after Holmes was sent to prison and unable to film. Related Stories Movies Ben Stiller Gives Update on His New York Knicks Documentary: "The Pressure Is on" Movies Elizabeth Holmes' Husband Billy Evans Claims He Didn't Consent to 'You Can See Everything' Nude Shower Scene

At a FYC event for East of Eden on Friday, Abbott told The Hollywood Reporter that Fielder and Oppenheim “just called me and asked me to come mess around. I got to see some of the footage they had shot before I did it, so it was a very quick run-and-gun thing, for me at least. I’ve been a fan of both of them for a long time so I kind of said yes before they even told me what they wanted to do.”

As for his take on the real Billy Evans, Abbott said he’s “heard about some of the craziness” but “I didn’t really know of him until they showed me the footage. I just thought it was a very interesting character to try to — I didn’t dive deep. I had just enough time to maybe try to do some version of mimicry or find little nuances. He’s an interesting subject.”

He also kept the appearance very hush-hush, as East of Eden co-showrunner Zoe Kazan — who is longtime friends with Abbott and was on the show’s press tour with him as the doc was starting to generate buzz — had no idea he was in the film.

“I’ve known Chris since we were in our early 20s coming up in the New York theater, and I went to see You Can See Everything with two people who’ve also known Chris for a long time, really well. And the three of us screamed in the theater when he came on screen, none of us knew,” Kazan said. “We sent him selfies with the poster afterwards. But I was really shocked.”

You Can See Everything has gone on to break box office records and generate lots of Oscar buzz, which Abbott noted is “amazing, especially for that type of film. Documentaries don’t get that type of attention,” but chalked it up to that “not only was the subject sort of juicy and accessible, they’re both really good filmmakers so they made it very cinematic.”

entertainment.title: Top Chef Alum Leah Cohen’s Husband Ben Byruch Dead at 44
entertainment.summary: Leah Cohen and her family are facing a devastating loss. Ben Byruch—a restaurateur and husband to the Top Chef alum—has died at the age of 44, their company Pig and Khao, which they co-founded,...
entertainment.body:
Ben Byruch —a restaurateur and husband to the Top Chef alum—has died at the age of 44, their company Pig and Khao, which they co-founded, shared Nov. 12.

“We are heartbroken to share the passing of Ben Byruch—husband to our chef and owner Leah Cohen, devoted father, son, brother, and friend to so many,” they wrote in a statement shared to Instagram . “Ben was the co-founder of Pig & Khao and its creative heart. His vision shaped who we are, and his warmth, passion and sense of humor touched everyone lucky enough to know him.”

The restaurant noted, “We ask for privacy for Leah and the family during this time. We will miss him more than words can say.”

Cohen—who ultimately placed sixth on the fifth season of Top Chef in 2008—tied the knot with Byruch in July 2016. Three years later, the couple welcomed their oldest son Carter , followed by their youngest son Baker in 2022.

The Great American Recipe judge previously opened up about working alongside her husband to build their businesses within the culinary world.

"Ben was actually hired as my line cook when we first opened and was quickly promoted to sous chef based on his skills," she told Downtown Magazine in 2016. "He was my sous chef for about a year until he made the switch to front of house. It’s much better for our relationship that we aren’t directly working together in the kitchen."

Cohen also shared what made their relationship work both on a professional and personal level.

“It can definitely be hard working with your significant other, but we do a good job of keeping business and personal lives separate,” she continued. “We try not to bring home any work drama, and if we do, we just let it out and then move on.”

entertainment.title: 9-1-1: Nashville Star Jessica Capshaw Played An Important Bones Character
entertainment.summary: Back in 2006, Jessica Capshaw appeared in a couple of episodes of Bones alongside David Boreanaz. Here's what she said about it years later.
entertainment.body:
Jake Giles Netter/Disney Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Since ending her 10-season run on "Grey's Anatomy," Jessica Capshaw has become even more of a familiar face to TV fans these days thanks to her starring role on the "9-1-1" spinoff series "9-1-1: Nashville." The actress plays Blythe Hart, the wife of fire captain Don Hart Jr. (Chris O'Donnell) and mother of Ryan Hart (Michael Provost). But this is far from the first time she's played an important mother on a cable drama series. Back in 2006, Capshaw made a brief but significant appearance on the fan-favorite TV show "Bones," starring David Boreanaz and Emily Deschanel .

The "9-1-1: Nashville" actress appears in two episodes as the character Rebecca Stinson, who had a previous relationship with Seeley Booth (Boreanaz). Their romance led to the birth of their son, Parker. At the beginning of Season 2, the show delves into their history when Booth grows suspicious of Stinson's new boyfriend and wary of their son spending time with him. A few episodes later, Temperance "Bones" Brennan (Deschanel) learns about Booth and Stinson sleeping together and investigates whether or not they want to get back together, and why Stinson didn't accept Booth's marriage proposal when she got pregnant years ago.

Capshaw only ever appears in two episodes of "Bones," but her character and her storyline help fans learn a lot more about Booth as a person, as well as how he is in romantic relationships. Stinson is mentioned again in Season 3, while her son with Booth, Parker, plays a bigger role in later seasons.

Fox In a retrospective interview about her "Bones" appearance on the "Boneheads" podcast with Emily Deschanel and Carla Gallo, Jessica Capshaw shared a bit about what led to her role on the hit TV show. She bluntly declared, "It was all David [Boreanaz]," before recounting their history and how it all went down. Capshaw explained that the two became friends after starring in the horror film "Valentine" together in 2001, and they remained close after. So when the role of Seeley Booth's ex came up on "Bones," Boreanaz thought his friend would be perfect for the part.

The podcast hosts and Capshaw went on to talk about her character, Rebecca Stinson, and the storyline of her and Booth's right-love-wrong-time relationship. Capshaw explained, "It wasn't for lack of love and coming together, but it just wasn't in the cards." The two still continue to co-parent Parker as "Bones" goes on, and as far as fans know, there are no issues later.

entertainment.title: How To Watch The 2026 Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards
entertainment.summary: Here's everything you need to know about the 2026 Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards, including where and how you can watch it.
entertainment.body:
The popular awards show dates back to 1987. The inaugural event was shown on the movie review series "Rated K: For Kids by Kids" and was originally known as "The Big Ballot." The following year, it was renamed the Kids' Choice Awards and was televised with live hosts, celebrity guests, and lots of slime.

This year's famous guests could be drenched in Nickelodeon's iconic green slime at any given moment, a tradition that's become a big part of the ceremony. Read on to find out who's going to be there, when the ceremony airs, and everything else we know about the 2026 Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards.

While the month of the show has never been set in stone, in the modern era, the Kids' Choice Awards have typically been held on a Saturday evening, when younger viewers tend to have more leeway when it comes to staying up late. It will run for one hour and 30 minutes in total, coming to a close at 9:30 p.m. ET and 6:30 p.m. PT.

Previously, the ceremony has taken place at a variety of venues, including the Barker Hangar, the Microsoft Theater, USC's Galen Center, The Forum, UCLA's Pauley Pavilion, the Hollywood Bowl, the Grand Olympic Auditorium, the Pantages Theatre, and Universal Studios Hollywood.

The Kids' Choice Awards have also taken place in other cities a few times over the years. In 1994, a special east coast portion of the show was shot at Universal Studios in Orlando, Florida, and in 1996, parts of the show were shot aboard the S.S. Nickelodeon in New York Harbor. Historically, however, it's very much an L.A. thing.

entertainment.title: Why Bruce Buffer Traded the Octagon for the Steakhouse in New Bud Light Campaign
entertainment.summary: The UFC ring announcer stars in a new Bud Light spot, as the beer brand and Omaha Steaks launch a new fan engagement play.
entertainment.body:
As the UFC returns to Madison Square Garden Saturday night, UFC ring announcer Bruce Buffer is trading the octagon for a steakhouse in a new Bud Light spot.

The campaign sees Buffer swap places with a steakhouse server so they can watch the big UFC fight, leaving him to serve the customers.

“I love when I perform or even when I’m doing commercials to be self-deprecating,” Buffer tells The Hollywood Reporter about the spot. “I like making fun of myself and just having fun for comedy purposes, and the creative people at Bud Light, you know, when they send me the storyboards, I go, ‘This is going to be awesome.’ So I totally dug my teeth into it. I loved it.” Related Stories Movies Ben Stiller Gives Update on His New York Knicks Documentary: "The Pressure Is on" Business Why Jordan Brand Is Using a 'Space Jam' Docuseries to Launch "Jordan TV"

The Bud Light spot was released ahead of UFC 334, which will take place tonight at Madison Square Garden in New York City. Bud Light is an official sponsor of UFC, with its spots typically running during the broadcast both for viewers and those in the arena.

“Bud Light’s creative team is just really fantastic at what they do, and looking at that, I trust them to come up with what they came up with, and they also give me the freedom to give feedback,” says Buffer. “It’s really, really cool, and it’s great when you work with people that are that comfortable to work with and respect the fact that they’re not damaging your brand, but yet enhancing it.”

In addition to the spot, Bud Light is partnering with UFC and Omaha Steaks on a “Fight Night Feast” package, which will bundle tomahawk steaks, Bud Light beer money, a Paramount+ gift card and UFC training gloves for $99.

“We know the best part of fight night is getting together with friends over an ice-cold Bud Light and some great food,” said Todd Allen, senior VP of marketing for Bud Light at Anheuser-Busch. “And with UFC 335 set to close out the year, we wanted to create something for UFC fans that makes fight night easy to enjoy. Fight Night Feast delivers everything needed for an unforgettable night of UFC action directly to fans’ doorsteps.”

But it’s also a testament to how far UFC has come. What was once an outcast sport now counts America’s biggest beer brand as a sponsor.

entertainment.title: Why Henry Cavill Left The Witcher
entertainment.summary: Henry Cavill's departure from The Witcher came as quite the shock back in 2022. So, why did he leave Netflix's dark fantasy series, and what did he do next?
entertainment.body:
Netflix Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Fans of Netflix's "The Witcher" were in for a major shock in 2022, when Henry Cavill departed the lead role of Geralt of Rivia after three seasons ; he was replaced by Liam Hemsworth. The cause of Cavill's departure wasn't initially clear, but more details surfaced before too long.

Although Cavill himself has not publicly explained why he left the dark fantasy series, showrunner Lauren Hissrich shared her view of the situation during a 2025 interview with Entertainment Weekly . "He had plans for other roles that he really wanted to commit himself to," Hissrich said of Cavill's decision to quit the show ahead of Season 4. "And for us, you don't want to hold someone and force them to be doing something that they don't want to do. I think that's why it felt like a really symbiotic decision."

After leaving "The Witcher," Cavill primarily focused on movies, taking lead roles in action films like "Argylle" and "The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare". As for what's next, the British actor is taking another stab at a video game adaptation, having landed the lead role in Prime Video's upcoming "Warhammer 40,000" series . Cavill has a number of additional projects in the works, including Chad Stahelski's "Highlander" reboot.

Katalin Vermes/Netflix Henry Cavill's abrupt departure from "The Witcher" didn't totally upend the series' production, as Liam Hemsworth's casting was announced at the same time. Even so, many viewers expressed their strong disappointment in the wake of the news, as Cavill's Geralt was widely deemed to be an excellent portrayal of the book and video game character.

Meanwhile, Cavill's "Witcher" co-star Freya Allan, who plays Geralt's adopted daughter Ciri on the show, didn't have an easy time processing Cavill's exit. In a 2025 interview with NME , Allan revealed that she only learned that Cavill was leaving right before the news broke publicly. She even considered quitting "The Witcher" for a time before finally deciding to complete her character's arc. "I cried because I wanted to finish the show with the guy that played my adoptive father," she said. "For the first time, I was seeing what life away from 'The Witcher' could look like and then the lead moves on ... He was the Geralt I grew up with."

Hemsworth's debut as the new Geralt on "The Witcher" garnered a mostly positive reception, though Season 4 ended up the lowest-rated chapter of the series to date, according to Rotten Tomatoes scores. "The Witcher" is set to conclude with Season 5, which will premiere on Netflix at some point in 2027.

entertainment.title: Can Chris Van Hollen Really Unseat Chuck Schumer?
entertainment.summary: Support for the Maryland Democrat is growing as he challenges the establishment mainstay's reign in the Senate
entertainment.body:
The day after the Democrats notched the most impressive electoral performance by either political party in a generation, Chuck Schumer kicked off his own campaign, racing to shore up enough support to continue leading Democrats when they reclaim control of the Senate in January. His rationale was simple: He should be made majority leader because his efforts — recruiting and raising funds — created the new majority.

In podcast and television appearances, as well as an Atlantic story declaring him the “architect of a historic landslide,” Schumer made a point to emphasize his role in flipping several hard-fought seats, including in Mississippi, a state he boasted had long been his “white whale.” Schumer told told The Daily he scouted Scott Colom personally: “I went to him and said, ‘You’ve got to run.’’

But Schumer’s argument is undermined by the fact that many of the incoming senators disagree with the characterization that he contributed much to their victories at all.

Speaking to The Washington Post last week before his race was called, Colom ran through a long list of Democrats who helped him become the first Black senator to represent Mississippi since Reconstruction. Sens. Sheldon Whitehouse and Raphael Warnock, former Vice President Kamala Harris, and former President Bill Clinton were on that list; Schumer, the Post wrote, was “notably absent.” Colom was even more explicit on Friday, telling CBS it was “not accurate” to say that Schumer recruited him. “The people of Mississippi recruited me… You think I was listening to someone that lives in Brooklyn?” He declined to say whether he would back Schumer for majority leader.

Colom is not alone. Of 13 incoming Democrats, only Sherrod Brown, the once and future senator of Ohio, has publicly pledged to support the Senate’s current Democratic leader.

Abdul El-Sayed, the newly elected senator from Michigan, threw his support behind Schumer’s rival Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland shortly after Van Hollen publicly announced his bid to challenge the senator from New York on Thursday. Van Hollen, who represented the D.C. suburbs in the U.S. House for a decade and half before joining the Senate in 2017, won praise in 2025 for traveling to El Salvador and demanding to meet with a constituent, Kilmar Abrego Garcia, who was erroneously sent by the Trump administration to the sprawling CECOT prison complex. You may recognize Imrie from playing Pamela Adlon's kooky mom on "Better Things" (or perhaps her iconic turn on the U.K.'s "Celebrity Traitors"), but she's truly in her element here as Budgie, the whip-smart attorney tasked with representing Sienna Miller's Carla in divorce court. Imrie took center stage this week as Budgie eloquently and entertainingly made her case in the courtroom... and we can't speak for the judge, but we were convinced.

Imrie's small stature and kewpie-doll smile might make her look like a pushover, but when it came time for Budgie's opening statement, she roared like a lion, efficiently laying the rhetorical groundwork for Carla's side while adding with a wink that she's a big fan of Carla's acting work... but "don't tell her I told you." It's clear Budgie can lay on the charm, but that's just her way of disarming you while she goes for the jugular, and Imrie flashed a lethal killer instinct as Budgie cross-examined Carla's estranged husband Morgan.

After softening him up with warm-up questions — and amusingly wondering if she can say "snagging" in a romantic sense these days without getting canceled — Budgie brought up the creation of Morgan's social media platform Zephyr and Carla's role in creating it. Carla had just suffered a vicious round of cyberbullying when Morgan came up with the idea for a more positive platform, and Budgie zeroes in on that fact, pointing out that Carla must've influenced Zephyr's creation in some way. Morgan bristled at Budgie's approach, angrily asking at one point if she had an actual question for him — and Imrie grinned as Budgie replied, "Not yet... but don't hesitate if you want to interrupt."

We don't know yet who will win the legal battle between Carla and Morgan, but we know Imrie has once again won our hearts with her sparkling turn as Budgie. entertainment.title: Why Captain Don Hart From 9-1-1: Nashville Looks So Familiar
entertainment.summary: If you recognize the actor who plays Captain Don Hart in "9-1-1: Nashville," that's because he's been a star of the big and small screen for decades.
entertainment.body:
Disney/Jake Giles Netter Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The part of firehouse chief Captain Don Hart in the ABC procedural drama "9-1-1: Nashville" is played by Chris O'Donnell. Much like co-stars Kimberly Williams-Paisley and Season 2 addition Ryan Phillippe , O'Donnell has been a familiar face on both the big and small screen for decades. After getting his start with a guest role in an episode of the '80s comedy drama series "Jack and Mike," he shifted his focus to feature films and set off on a journey that would take him to the A-list.

O'Donnell made his feature debut in the 1990 dramedy "Men Don't Leave" starring Jessica Lange and Kathy Bates, and the following year he played the role of Buddy Threadgoode in the Oscar-nominated drama "Fried Green Tomatoes," reuniting with Bates. His breakout role was right around the corner: O'Donnell's performance as prep school student Charlie Simms in the 1992 Al Pacino film "Scent of a Woman" earned him a Golden Globe nomination for best supporting actor.

In 1993, O'Donnell continued his rise as D'Artagnan in the swashbuckling adventure "The Three Musketeers" with Kiefer Sutherland and Charlie Sheen. Two years later, he masked up as Dick Grayson (aka Robin) in Joel Schumacher's "Batman Forever" alongside Val Kilmer's Bruce Wayne. He reprised the role in 1997 for the critically slammed "Batman & Robin," which saw George Clooney taking over as the Caped Crusader.

Disney/Jake Giles Netter By the mid-2000s, Chris O'Donnell had dipped a toe back into TV, with a memorable guest-starring role in "Two and a Half Men" among the earliest credits from his small screen renaissance era. In the years that followed he charmed viewers as veterinarian Dr. Finn Dandridge — Meredith Grey's beau — in a major arc on "Grey's Anatomy" and he tackled the spy thriller genre as Jack McCauliffe in the acclaimed Cold War miniseries "The Company." Of course, his biggest TV role prior to "9-1-1: Nashville" was Special Agent in Charge Grisha "G" Callen on "NCIS: Los Angeles," a character he originated on the mothership series "NCIS." O'Donnell also appeared in an episode of "NCIS: Hawai'i" during his stint as Callen, which ran from 2009 to 2023.

O'Donnell didn't intend on going straight into another network procedural when "NCIS: Los Angeles" came to an end in 2023, but then Ryan Murphy got in touch about a "9-1-1" spin-off set in Nashville. "Having just done 14 years in Los Angeles — which was the greatest gift of all time, and that show came up when I had five kids in school — and given that my town had just burned to the ground, picking up and moving to Nashville almost sounded too good to be true, frankly," O'Donnell told TV Guide . "I just put my faith in Ryan and his team that they would come up with interesting things, and I was ready to go." O'Donnell also revealed that "9-1-1: Lone Star" alum Rob Lowe helped persuade him to take the "9-1-1: Nashville" gig .

entertainment.title: '70s Icon James Brolin's '90s Action Series Flopped Despite A Major Network Push
entertainment.summary: James Brolin's career hit a few roadbumps during the 1990s - including one ill-fated action series, which ABC placed in a very special spot on the schedule.
entertainment.body:
William Nation/Getty & undefined Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover James Brolin was a TV and film legend, but the '90s marked a turbulent time for his career. Brolin rose to fame in the '70s after starring in the forgotten Emmy-winning medical drama "Marcus Welby, M.D." This led to his first and only Emmy and sparked his successful career as a Hollywood leading man. But in the early '90s, Brolin ended up appearing in a series of flops, including the short-lived action series "Extreme."

The series followed a search-and-rescue team in Utah, with Brolin playing Reese Wheeler, the unit's fatherly leader. The show also featured a former Miss America, Elizabeth Gracen, future "That '70s Show" star Danny Masterson, and Julie Bowen, who would become an Emmy winner for her work on "Modern Family." Since Brolin had starred in "Marcus Welby, M.D.," ABC's first No. 1 show on the Nielsen rankings, the network had high hopes for "Extreme," even slotting its premiere directly after the Super Bowl in 1995.

That strategy had previously worked for ABC with "The Wonder Years," turning that show into an instant hit. But plenty of TV series have also flopped after premiering in the wake of the Super Bowl. In the case of "Extreme," it was not a success story, and ABC gave up on the series before its season finale. Only seven episodes ever aired.

Steve Granitz/Getty The low viewership for "Extreme" was a surprise for ABC, since the series had passed its test screening with flying colors. "I had two series that tested (just) OK that went to No. 1 within six weeks," Brolin told the Morning Call in 1995, after "Extreme" was ranked 78th on the Nielsen charts. "This one tested brilliantly right from the beginning. ... You never know." There are two reasons why the show might have failed to resonate with audiences.

Firstly, ABC fumbled the release schedule, airing the rest of the season two months after the premiere, which lost any momentum that may have been gained from the Super Bowl release. The show was also scheduled on the same evening as hit NBC sitcoms "Friends" and "Seinfeld," making it even harder to win over audiences.

The second reason was that the series was a little bland, leading to harsh reviews. The New York Daily News ' headline read: "Premise of Brolin Series is 'Extreme'ly dumb." Meanwhile, Variety wrote, "The inane dialogue and laborious character development obfuscate the high points, making this series bow heavy with lengthy bouts of boredom punctuated by moments of high excitement." There's no direct evidence for what general audiences thought about the series, but perhaps they felt similar, since it received such a low turnout. Luckily, Brolin recovered his reputation as a TV star with his next series, "Pensacola: Wings of Gold," which lasted three seasons.

entertainment.title: 10 TV Shows To Watch If You Like Dark Winds
entertainment.summary: Dark Winds is one of the best AMC shows ever made and a phenomenal neo-Western. Here are 10 similar shows fans should check out immediately.
entertainment.body:
Michael Moriatis/AMC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

One of the best AMC TV shows , certainly in the past several years, is "Dark Winds," which premiered in 2022. A pulp neo-Western thriller, the show is based on the "Leaphorn & Chee" novels by Tony Hillerman, with each season adapting a different book. While set in the 1970s on and around an Indigenous reservation in the American Southwest, the show doesn't feel like a period piece, instead focused on delivering intensely crafted mysteries. The impressive ensemble cast is led by Zahn McClarnon, who also executive produces the series, as the driven tribal police officer Joe Leaphorn.

While we wait for the next season of "Dark Winds," there are plenty of other shows that provide their own crime thriller action. More than just procedurals, the shows that we're mentioning here also veer into neo-Western and neo-noir thematic territory. Several of these series also delve into the social issues facing Indigenous communities and prominently feature Indigenous characters. These are 10 TV shows to watch if you like "Dark Winds" and are looking for something similar.

FX Networks Arguably the show that powered the neo-Western genre's resurgence on television, "Justified" is a creative tour-de-force. Based on author Elmore Leonard's crime stories about protagonist Raylan Givens, Timothy Olyphant makes the role his own in the series. The show opens with Raylan, a quick-draw U.S. Marshal, reassigned to his hometown in Kentucky, a region that he has plenty of unresolved angst towards. Leading with his proactive sense of justice, Raylan goes head-to-head with several criminal organizations in the area, often putting his gunslinging skills to the test.

"Justified" is easily one of the best neo-Western TV shows of all time , so let's get it out of the way first. The show is sharply written from top-to-bottom and driven by its character dynamics, especially between Raylan and resident ne'er-do-well Boyd Crowder (Walton Goggins). More for the purposes of this list's comparative premise, the show depicts small-town crime in an engaging way while highlighting the toll that it takes on Raylan's personal life. Among the best shows ever produced for FX , "Justified" remains thoroughly enjoyable over a decade after its conclusion.

Warner Bros. Television Another show based on a pulp neo-Western novel series, "Longmire" adapts the "Walt Longmire Mysteries" by Craig Johnson . The series' title character is a small-town sheriff in Wyoming, played by Robert Taylor, grieving the death of his wife. Because of his jurisdiction's proximity to a reservation, Walt frequently consults with his best friend Henry Standing Bear (Lou Diamond Phillips) when working with tribal police. Joining the ensemble is Walt's daughter Cady (Cassidy Freeman), solving crimes in and around the Cheyenne reservation while trying to move on with their lives.

Kylie Jenner’s legal troubles could get even worse as more former employees are preparing to sue the reality star.

“There are more lawsuits against Kylie coming. This isn’t the end,” a source exclusively told Page Six. “The claims are substantially similar to the current lawsuits.”

The warning came after the Kylie Cosmetics founder was hit with four separate lawsuits from former household employees in just seven months.

The women, who worked as housekeepers and a private chef at Jenner’s properties, accused the beauty mogul and members of her staff of discrimination, harassment, wrongful termination and numerous labor violations.

Their allegations included claims that one employee was trapped inside Jenner’s closet, another was forced to hide whenever “The Kardashians” star was home, and a pregnant chef who suffered a miscarriage after allegedly being required to perform physically demanding work.

Jenner’s legal representative Michael Rhodes previously denied the allegations against the entrepreneur, telling Page Six in a statement, “These latest cases are being brought by the same lawyer who previously filed claims on behalf of Kylie’s former household staff. It’s clear that this lawyer wants to use publicity to try and extract an unwarranted payday.”

He added, “We’re not going to be intimidated into doing that. As such, we’ll defend these meritless cases vigorously and look forward to telling our side of the story.”

Meanwhile, attorney Della Shaker, who represents all four former employees, fired back in a statement shared with Page Six, “We are here to protect rights, not reputations. And we will not back down.”

entertainment.title: ‘Is This Supposed to Happen?’: How Matt Dike Dominated Eighties Hip-Hop Music
entertainment.summary: Peter Relic details a wild night in LA with Delicious Vinyl's co-founders Matt Dike, Michael Ross, and rapper Tone Loc in this excerpt from his book Bust a Move , out now
entertainment.body:
Set in 1980s Los Angeles, Peter Relic’s “ Bust a Move: Matt Dike, Delicious Vinyl, and the Hip-Hop Hits that First Conquered Pop ” chronicles the peculiar circumstances that led to the founding of independent record label Delicious Vinyl, and the creation of three of the biggest crossover singles of that era: “Wild Thing” and “Funky Cold Medina” by Tone Loc, and Young MC’s “Bust a Move.”

“The fact that those indelible hits — as well as Beastie Boys’ classic album ‘Paul’s Boutique’ — were created in Matt Dike’s dusty, second floor apartment using patched-together equipment makes this one of the great DIY success stories in music history,” Relic, a Rolling Stone and Vibe contributor says . “I had no idea how truly extraordinary this story would be going into it, never mind how the mystery of Matt Dike would drive my entire investigation.”

As the record label Dike cofounded with fellow nightclub DJ Michael Ross rose to global prominence, the charismatic producer was offered the chance to work with artists including Aerosmith and Brian Wilson. Instead, Matt Dike disappeared.

“All I had was his phone number, and the knowledge that Matt had not given an in-person interview to the press since 1990. What I never guessed was what was going to happen that night after he finally picked up the phone.”

In the following excerpt from the book, three of the key players find themselves at a miraculous, ridiculous tipping point in hip-hop and pop music history.

Tone Loc was stuck. Like a big, brawny genie trapped in a dusty bottle, the rapper in the wraparound shades needed to be freed to unleash his magic.

Here, onstage at the Fabulous Forum in Inglewood, California, with purple-and-gold Los Angeles Lakers championship banners dangling from the rafters and 18,000 teenyboppers baying for beats, the semi-reformed gangster could only blink through the tendrils of dry ice swirling around him, his heart thumping faster than the tom-tom turnaround of his big hit “Wild Thing.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

entertainment.title: Stephen King's Cult 5-Season Sci-Fi Detective Series Is Streaming For Free
entertainment.summary: Is there really a show that brings together Pennywise, Shawshank, and the Overlook Hotel? Honestly, no - but this Stephen King series is as close as you'll get.
entertainment.body:
SYFY Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Among the myriad movies and shows based on Stephen King stories , "Haven" stands out for linking a number of his novels together. And this cult series is now available to watch for free online.

"Haven" was initially developed as an adaptation of King's 2005 novella "The Colorado Kid," a murder mystery about a body found on the coast of Maine hours after the victim bought a cigarette in Colorado, halfway across the country. Rather than directly adapting the story, however, "Haven" creators Sam Ernst and Jim Dunn drew on the novella's mysterious vibe to make a supernatural detective drama. The five-season series follows FBI agent Audrey Parker, who is sent to Haven, Maine, to solve a mystery — but instead comes face-to-face with paranormal events, known in the series as "The Troubles."

Parker stays to help the police department protect the townspeople from the Troubles and each other, and she soon discovers that her past somehow links to Haven itself. But the show is far more than an adaptation of "The Colorado Kid." Across the show's five seasons, there are multiple easter eggs from King's novels and novellas, including references to Shawshank Prison, Pennywise the Dancing Clown, and even the tricycle from "The Shining." If you're a fan of King's books — or supernatural mystery shows like "The X-Files" or "Supernatural" — you will love this series, which you can stream for free on YouTube, The Roku Channel, Pluto TV, The CW, and Plex.

SYFY Speaking to The Philadelphia Inquirer in 2010, Sam Ernst explained that "Haven" was initially a direct adaptation of "The Colorado Kid." "Initially, our idea was to stay close to the book, so it had no supernatural element," Ernst said (via The Ventura Country Star ). "But when King read it, the first thing he said was, 'Where's the supernatural element?'" So, they changed the series into a monster-of-the-week show, in which each episode follows a different townsperson facing a supernatural problem.

Though "Haven" enjoyed strong ratings to begin with, critics did not receive the early seasons well. The first season holds a Rotten Tomatoes critic score of 35%, with critics saying the show is too bland and feels like a poor copy of other supernatural horror TV shows . Later seasons received more praise from critics, eventually reaching 80% on Rotten Tomatoes in Seasons 4 and 5 (albeit from only a handful of reviews in each case).

entertainment.title: 5 Years Ago Today: Taylor Sheridan Launched A Hit TV Drama Outside The Yellowstone Universe
entertainment.summary: It's been five years since Taylor Sheridan released this hit TV drama outside the Yellowstone universe, and the journey from concept to end has been a ride.
entertainment.body:
Created by Sheridan and Hugh Dillon, the show follows Mike McLusky (Jeremy Renner), who's the key to facilitating a peaceful balance between criminals and law enforcement around the town of Kingstown, Michigan, "where incarceration is its biggest business" (via Paramount+ ). He was thrust into the dangerous position after the murder of his brother Mitch (Kyle Chandler), who wielded great power in town. Of course, that was only the start of the drama for Mike, who's spent the last four seasons navigating the increasingly volatile setup.

Season 5 of "Mayor of Kingstown" will premiere on January 15, 2027. In addition to Renner, Season 5 will also star Nichole Galicia, Edie Falco, David Morse, Laura Benanti, Taylor Handley, Tobi Bamtefa, and Derek Webster, along with several more.

Paramount+ The mostly rewatchable "Yellowstone" may have preceded "Mayor of Kingstown" by several years, but Taylor Sheridan actually wrote the latter first. He made this admission while discussing his pivot from acting to writing. "If you're banging your head against the wall for 20 years trying to be an actor, maybe you shouldn't be an actor," he told The Hollywood Reporter in 2023. Then came a shift. "But the first thing I ever wrote [the pilot for "Mayor of Kingstown" in 2011] got me meetings at every major network, at every agency. I had multiple people trying to buy it."

The path to selling the rights and actually getting the show made was anything but linear — especially because Sheridan, who's known to write most of his own material, was hesitant to give up creative control by letting "more experienced" writers bring his premise to life. But "Mayor of Kingstown" eventually became another popular series for him.

Unfortunately for fans, Season 5 will mark the end of "Mayor of Kingstown," but it's ending will likely be meticulously planned. According to Sheridan's co-creator, Hugh Dillon, Sheridan knew exactly how he wanted "Mayor of Kingstown" to end from the beginning. "We had it before, where we sold the script. Taylor had it. Taylor had it in his head," Dillon shared with ScreenRant when discussing their script-writing process. "We talked about how the whole thing goes, and this is where it's going to end in whatever season it ends, but that's part of what the fun was, because then we can fill in the rest of it, because we know where it's ending."

entertainment.title: Michael J. Fox Had A Real-Life Inspiration For Family Ties' Alex P. Keaton
entertainment.summary: Michael J. Fox's audition for the role of Alex P. Keaton in Family Ties was a big deal for the young actor. Luckily, he knew just where to find his inspiration.
entertainment.body:
During a May 2001 interview with the Television Academy , Fox opened up about his uphill battle to secure the role of Alex in NBC's hit family sitcom . He revealed that, ahead of his audition, he'd channeled his own flesh and blood to nail the character's signature cadence and sharp wit. "I got it. I understood it. I knew how to make it funny," Fox recalled. "I was basically just playing my brother, who was the smarta** in our family, who was so much smarter than everybody else."

Fox noted that, while he hadn't quite mastered comedic timing at that point in his career, he did pick up a few pointers by watching how his brother held everyone's attention around the dinner table. "He'd put his glass of milk down, and from the minute he took the glass away from his mouth, you were waiting for what he had to say," he shared. "So, later on, that all became part of Alex, so I just knew that as I was auditioning. I just got it. There was just a sense that I had — that that was it."

"So I went and I read that second time, and I could tell right away he was laughing," Fox recalled to the Television Academy. "He's laughing, and I know I'm scoring, and now I'm learning this thing that I didn't really know because I hadn't done that much of this level of sitcom — feeding on the laugh and playing up the expectation that he had, and the more he laughs the more I know what he likes, and I hit that harder the next time."

After Fox nailed that second audition, Goldberg turned to Weiner, asking her why nobody ever told him how good the actor was; Fox later recalled that, from then on, the showrunner was his biggest champion. Not long after "Family Ties" turned him into a household name — the era-defining NBC series aired for seven seasons from 1982 to 1989 — Fox catapulted to stratospheric fame when he landed his role as Marty McFly in 1985's "Back to the Future," fully cementing his status as a pop culture icon.

Bryan Cranston brought an added poignancy to the Alzheimer’s-themed cartoon “Tangles,” because his mom suffered from the disease.

“My mother had Alzheimer’s,” he told Page Six exclusively at a screening of the well-reviewed movie earlier this week. “So I knew what that was like to step in.”

The “Breaking Bad” alum, 70, voices a man whose wife is diagnosed with the progressive brain disorder, along with Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Abbi Jacobson, Samira Wiley and Beanie Feldstein.

“I think everybody in the cast has had experience with Alzheimer’s,” he noted. “Close experiences. And so I knew what to expect from my character when it was diminishing, and to be able to then find those moments when he is — when my character is ultra vulnerable or strong or in denial or all the — you’re going through everything.”

Cranston shared that the disease “doesn’t progress naturally…it really takes you for a loop.”

His mother, Peggy Sell, raised Bryan and his two siblings after their father left the family. She suffered from alcoholism, and the actor did not always have an easy relationship with her.

Netflix Ten years after "The Crown" premiered its first season on Netflix, it remains the epitome of prestige TV. The award-winning series chronicles the history of the British royal family over nearly six decades of Queen Elizabeth's reign. Presenting a dramatized version of true events, all six seasons of "The Crown" are defined by their high production value, detailed depiction of historical eras, and stellar performances.

Led by Claire Foy, Matt Smith, and Vanessa Kirby for the first two seasons, "The Crown" enlisted tons of outstanding actors, including Olivia Colman, Josh O'Connor, and Elizabeth Debicki later on. "The Crown" Seasons 5 and 6 drew a lot more criticism for its creative liberties compared to previous runs, but showrunner Peter Morgan still managed to create engaging interpersonal conflict and in-depth examinations of real-life royals throughout the majority of "The Crown".

Even those uninterested in the affairs of Britain's most famous family should find "The Crown" an enjoyable viewing experience, as the series' strengths far outweigh the likability of its main characters.

Daniel Daza/Netflix "Narcos" is the perfect drama for anyone who loves history and wants an exhilarating gangster show . entertainment.title: ‘Fatherland,’ ‘La Bola Negra,’ ‘Fjord’ Lead European Film Award Nominations
entertainment.summary: Sandra Hüller scored a dual best actress nom for 'Fatherland' and 'Rose,' with Renate Reinsve, Sebastian Stan, Penelope Cruz, Javier Bardem and Andrew Scott among the acting nominees.
entertainment.body:
Pawel Pawlikowski’s German black-and-white period drama Fatherland , and La Bola Negra , a gay Spanish epic from director Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, are the frontrunners for the 2027 European Film Awards , with Fatherland racking up 11 EFA nominations to 10 for La Bola Negra .

Both Fatherland and La Bola Negra picked up EFA noms in the best European film, European director, European screenwriter and European cinematographer categories, with Fatherland also receiving European actress and European actor noms for leads Hanns Zischler and Sandra Hüller for their performances, respectively, as Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and daughter Erika. Related Stories Movies Modern Fairy Tale 'Mo Amor' Explores Identity, Transformation and Love in All Its Forms Movies 5 Takeaways From China's Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival

Hüller received a second best European actress nom, for her starring role as a 17th-century woman masquerading as a man in Markus Schleinzer’s Rose . She’s going up against Penélope Cruz , nominated for Florian Zeller’s Bunker ; Léa Seydoux for her leading role in Marie Kreutzer’s Gentle Monster ; Mathilde Arcel for her performance in May el-Toukhy’s Venice Festival winner Woman Unknown ; and Renate Reinsve for her starring role in Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or-winning Fjord .

Sebastian Stan , who plays Reinsve’s fundamentalist Christian husband in Fjord , received a best European actor nomination, alongside Zischler; Javier Bardem , nominated for Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s The Beloved ; Swann Arlaud for his turn in Emmanuel Marre’s A Man of His Time ; and Andrew Scott , nominated for his performance in Simon Stone’s Elsinore as Ian Charleson, the British actor dying of AIDS who throws himself into a final performance of Hamlet .

Nominated for best European film, alongside Fatherland and La Bola Negra , are Fjord , Woman Unknown and La Gradiva , a French coming-of-age drama from first-time director Marine Atlan.

Best European director nominees, alongside Pawlikowski and Ambrossi/Calvo, are Mungiu for Fjord , Sandra Wollner for the German drama Everytime and Andrey Zvyagintsev for the Russian crime thriller Minotaur .

The European Animation Film nominees are: In Waves , directed by Phuong Mai Nguyen; Iron Boy from Louis Clichy; Jim Queen , directed by Marco Nguyen and Nicolas Athané; Lucy Lost , directed by Olivier Clert; and Viva Carmen from Sébastien Laudenbach.

entertainment.summary: Steve Murphy will fill in for the rest of November, weeks after Castronovo suffered an onstage medical emergency in Tulsa.
entertainment.body:
Journey drummer Deen Castronovo is stepping away from the band’s farewell tour to deal with his health, the group announced Friday (Nov. 13).

“After careful consideration and an extensive year of touring , our talented, longtime drummer Deen Castronovo has decided to step away to focus on personal health matters that require his attention,” the band said in a statement. “He has our full support during this time and extends his heartfelt thanks to the fans for the love, encouragement, and kindness he has received.”

Steve Murphy will take over for the remainder of November. The New York drummer has previously worked with the Alan Parsons Project, Trans-Siberian Orchestra, Christopher Cross and Jack Bruce. The announcement follows a scare last month, when Castronovo was helped offstage and taken to hospital after two songs at Tulsa’s BOK Center on Oct. 8. He returned two nights later for a full show in San Antonio, and guitarist Neal Schon said at the time that he was “back in rare form.” Neither the band nor Castronovo has disclosed details of the illness.

Castronovo, 62, first joined Journey in 1998, replacing Steve Smith, and played on five albums before leaving in 2015. He returned in 2021, initially alongside Narada Michael Walden, and became the sole drummer after Walden’s 2022 departure. He also sings, occasionally taking lead vocals, and has played with Bad English, Hardline and Ozzy Osbourne.

His exit comes near the end of a long year on the road. The Final Frontier tour, promoted by AEG Presents, launched Feb. 28 in Hershey, Pa., with an initial 60 North American dates, before the band added 40 more for the fall. The current leg began Sept. 12 in Los Angeles. Keyboardist Jonathan Cain has said the run marks his own farewell chapter with the band, which also features founder Neal Schon, singer Arnel Pineda, keyboardist Jason Derlatka and bassist Todd Jensen.

The tour continues Saturday (Nov. 14) at Bon Secours Wellness Arena in Greenville, S.C., and wraps Nov. 28 at San Francisco’s Chase Center.

sports.title: Report: Vikings first reached out to Raiders about Kirk Cousins on "midday Monday"
sports.summary: As it turns out, the Vikings contacted the Raiders about a possible trade for quarterback Kirk Cousins before Monday night's meltdown from quarterback Carson Wentz.
sports.body:
Via ESPNFL, the Vikings initially contacted the Raiders during “midday Monday,” prior to Minnesota’s Week 9 game against the Bills. The Vikings told the Raiders they wanted to see how things went during the Monday night game before having any further conversations.

Then came Wentz’s 8.9-passer rating performance in a 23-6 loss, and Minnesota mobilized. The Vikings, per the report, contacted the Raiders before 6:00 a.m. PT on Tuesday and commenced the talks that culminated in a deal being done.

Said Raiders G.M. John Spytek during a Tuesday press conference: “I never made one call on Kirk Cousins. And I got a few phone calls. But one real one this morning .”

The Vikings initially offered a fifth-round pick for Cousins, per the report. The report doesn’t specify the Raiders’ opening position.

Once the Vikings moved to a third-round pick, the Raiders pounced.

Beyond avoiding the $10 million guaranteed bonus and clearing the path for rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza (which are mentioned in the article), the Raiders ultimately bought a third-round pick for $650,000 (which is not).

That’s the most attractive aspect of the entire transaction, in our view. Nearly 10 years ago, the Browns bought a second-round pick from the Texans by assuming quarterback Brock Osweiler’s $16 million full guarantee for the 2017 season. Any team would sprint for the chance to purchase a third-round pick in the 2027 draft for only $650,000.

In this case, that bargain came with nine starts from Cousins, four wins, and months of excellent mentorship for Mendoza.

sports.title: Ground stop results in side judge Don Willard serving as referee for two games on Sunday
sports.summary: Flight disruptions result in multiple changes to Week 10 officiating assignments.
sports.body:
The NFL has announced that officiating assignments have changed for Week 10. And the situation will result in a backup referee serving as the referee in two games on the same day.

“Due to the ongoing nationwide impact to air travel this weekend, the NFL has adjusted its officiating assignments for Week 10 games, reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns,” the NFL said in a statement. “The changes will necessitate that three backup referees — umpires Barry Anderson and Duane Heydt and side judge Don Willard [pictured] — will work as referees in the following games: Carolina-New Orleans – Duane Heydt; Jacksonville-Tennessee – Barry Anderson; Miami-Indianapolis and Pittsburgh-Cincinnati – Don Willard.

“Each of the league’s 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified, and that individual trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise.”

The situation creates the likely unprecedented situation of a referee working two games in one day. Willard will handle Dolphins-Colts at 1:00 p.m. ET, and then he’ll make the 109-mile trip from Indianapolis to Cincinnati for the Sunday night game.

Making the unprecedented even more unusual is the fact that Willard’s usual crew (led by referee Scott Novak) wasn’t scheduled to work at all this weekend.

The announcement doesn’t address where the referees for those three games will be working, or what their roles will be. Shawn Smith was scheduled to be the referee for Panthers-Saints, Alex Moore was set to be the referee for Jaguars-Titans, Carl Cheffers was due to be the referee for Dolphins-Colts, and Clete Blakeman was slated to be the referee for Steelers-Bengals.

The league’s statement also doesn’t specify other shifts that were required as to the established crews that work together throughout the regular season.

sports.title: Jerry Jones: "I don't think we're far away" from 18 regular-season games
sports.summary: As to the timeline, Jones says, "Next month? No. Next year? Maybe. [The] next year? Maybe."
sports.body:
It’s no secret that the NFL wants to expand the regular season from 17 to 18 games. The league is sufficiently confident about it happening that folks like Cowboys owner Jerry Jones speak of it as a given.

“ I don’t think we’re far away from it ,” Jones said Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, regarding the addition of an extra game. “I don’t know how — what is far away. Next month? No. Next year? Maybe. [The] next year? Maybe. That has to be negotiated with the players.

“But it’s in everybody’s best interests. You’d cut back on the preseason games. You’d have teams more develop in the first few games as the type of thing you were trying to get done in preseason. But it’s in everybody’s interest, and it certainly is in the players’ best interest in my mind, for sure. And having said that, I would anticipate that coming.”

His comments presume the NFL Players Association will happily agree to 18 regular-season games. They likely won’t. At a minimum, they’ll seek major concessions in exchange for the willingness to add yet another game that counts.

The unspoken goal had been 2027. The NFL delayed picking a date for Super Bowl LXII in Atlanta in order to accommodate the possibility that the game will slide a week or two deeper into February. That would make 2028 the earliest year for expansion, as a practical matter. (Adding a game for 2027 would be possible only if the dead week between the conference championships is wiped out or if the season starts a week earlier. If an 18th game will result in a second bye, both would be required.)

Expansion by 2027 would require expedited negotiations. Expansion by 2028 would hinge on the NFL and NFLPA striking a deal within the next year or so. The union has shown no inclination, however, to engage in talks aimed at extending the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, which runs through the 2030 season.

Still, if push comes to shove, there will be 18 games. The blueprint was created in 2011. The NFL will lock the players out until the players agree to the things the owners want. Most notably, 18 regular-season games and 16 annual international games.

Beyond that, Jones’s comment about the early games of the season is odd. “ You’d have teams more develop in the first few games as the type of thing you were trying to get done in preseason. ”

sports.body: The Jets’ defense has had its issues in 2026, to say the least. However, there’s at least one area where they have improved. The defense as a whole has been a lot more opportunistic this year in terms of forcing fumbles. Led by David Bailey’s five, they have forced a total of 13 fumbles. That’s already four more than the total for all of last season. New York’s fumble luck has been a lot better too, as they’ve recovered 50 percent of all fumbles. This is much higher than their 2025 percentage, which was the second-worst in the league at 35 percent (and was actually on target to break the all-time record until they had a few over the last few weeks of the season). Had they been closer to 50 percent last year, or 2023 when they were dead last in fumble recovery percentage, or 2022 when they were 30th, those seasons could arguably have played out very differently. 2023 in particular was particularly galling, as the Jets started 7-4 and then lost their last six as the turnovers dried up. They almost tied the all-time NFL record for the fewest defensive fumble recoveries until Carl Lawson ended a nine-game drought by recovering one with two games remaining. In the end, they only managed to recover 21 percent of fumbles by opposing offenses. It’s often been debated how much of fumble recovery percentages are dictated by talent and how much is based on luck, with most analytical studies concluding it’s mostly luck. However, if you have a team that is hungry and hustles to the ball, has players who are particularly adept at possessing loose balls or are creating the kinds of fumbles which are more likely to be recovered by the defense, this obviously has an effect on some level. sports.title: Jared Goff takes 1-3 career record vs. Patriots into Germany game
sports.summary: For his career, Lions quarterback Jared Goff has a record of 101-67-1 as a starter.
sports.body:
Against the Patriots, Goff is 1-3. That’s a 25-percent win rate.

In those four games, Goff has two touchdown passes and five interceptions.

Sunday’s game in Germany will be the first one against the Patriots with a coach other than Bill Belichick. Goff has never faced current Patriots coach Mike Vrabel; during Goff’s time as a starter with the Rams and Lions and Vrabel’s tenure with the Titans, their two teams never crossed paths.

Goff’s first loss to New England came in 2016, in his third career start. The Patriots won, 26-10. Two years later, New England beat Goff and the Rams in the Super Bowl, 13-3.

In 2020, the Patriots beat Goff and the Rams, 24-3. In 2022, the Patriots beat Goff and the Lions, 29-0.

Sunday’s game is consequential for both teams. The 6-2 Lions are caught in a cluster of four NFC North teams that all have six or more wins. The Patriots, at 5-4, are fading in the AFC East race and could be scrambling to secure a wild-card spot.

sports.title: Kyle Shanahan: Mike Evans is getting better, we're trying to make sure he fully heals
sports.summary: The 49ers have ruled out wide receiver Mike Evans for Sunday's game in Dallas, but head coach Kyle Shanahan says Evans is getting healthy enough to play.
sports.body:
Evans is dealing with Achilles tendinitis and Shanahan said that while Evans’ recovery is progressing and he could probably play if he had to, the 49ers want to prioritize his long-term health and not the short-term benefit of having him on the field on Sunday.

“It’s been going well. I’m sure if this was the last game or something he’d be able to go out there, but we’re just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn’t act up again. But it’s going in the right direction,” Shanahan said.

Although Evans won’t play this week, Shanahan said Evans could be good to go for next week’s game, Sunday night against the Vikings in Mexico City.

“There’s a chance for next week, but not sure yet,” Shanahan said.

The 33-year-old Evans was off to an outstanding start this season, and he’s the 49ers’ team leader with an average of 70 receiving yards per game. The 49ers want to get that production back, but the top priority is having Evans produce in the playoffs.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills are Jersey bound, heading to East Rutherford to take on the New York Jets this week. It’s just the second divisional game for the Bills, as they have just their October loss vs. the New England Patriots on their AFC East ledger so far. The Jets, meanwhile, will finish their first go-rounds of AFC East games with Sunday’s matchup. While New York may be just 2-7 this season, they’ve played a lot of tight games, including two against the New England Patriots and Miami Dolphins. The Patriots defeated the Jets 26-19, while the Dolphins squeaked out a 28-25 victory. Really, the only game the Jets were entirely demolished in came last week, when they lost 35-12 against the Kansas City Chiefs. Can the Jets play the Bills tight this week? Will Buffalo overlook their division rivals and lose the game outright? There’s no question that Buffalo is the better football team, but there’s a reason why they play the games rather than just talking about them. The Bills will need to come out ready to roll in order to maintain their hold on the No. 1 seed in the AFC. Here are five Bills to watch on Sunday as they try to do just that. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Josh Allen Last week, after a slow start, Allen caught fire in the second half against an outstanding Minnesota Vikings defense. Allen started his night just 7-of-14 for 51 yards and an interception, but from the Bills’ two-minute drive at the end of the first half until the end of the game, he was electric. Allen completed 14 of his next 21 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown, and while those numbers might sound pedestrian, Allen finished his day as just the second quarterback to eclipse 200 yards passing against the Vikings this season. sports.title: Ground stop nudges Ole Miss-Oklahoma game to Sunday (and OU doesn't like that)
sports.summary: Friday's nationwide shutdown of the aviation system has resulted in a delayed kickoff for several college football games on Saturday.
sports.body:
The Ole Miss visit to Oklahoma shifted from 4:15 p.m. ET on Saturday to Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET.

“The Ole Miss football team was unable to depart Oxford Friday night due to the FAA ground stoppage,” the SEC said in a statement. “After the stoppage was lifted, a late-night departure could not be accommodated by the charter company with which Ole Miss was contracted and the team’s departure has been delayed until Saturday afternoon.”

Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny strenuously objected to the decision to move the game to Sunday.

“After multiple conversations with the league office, Commissioner [Greg] Sankey informed us of his decision to move our game to Sunday, over our strong objection,” Denny said. “He further informed us that our failure to play on Sunday at the directed time would result in a forfeit. I understand that difficult decisions sometimes must be made under extraordinary circumstances. But those decisions must also consider the impact on everyone involved. Put simply, this decision isn’t fair to our athletes, our institution, or to Sooner Nation.”

Oklahoma nevertheless will comply with the decision. Even if the Sooners don’t like the decision to play the game later.

“Rescheduling the game has a significant impact, particularly on our fans,” Denny said. “Those who have made travel arrangements, accommodations, and personal plans around a Saturday game now face unnecessary disruption and hardship. Their time, commitment, and investment deserve greater consideration than they were afforded in the conference’s decision tonight. . . . We are obligated to play the game when directed. But we remain steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening.”

On one hand, there’s no point huffing and puffing if Oklahoma ultimately wasn’t going to blow the house down. On the other hand, the school may have felt compelled to do something to deflect the frustrations of those who weren’t happy with having the game moved to the next day.

The bottom line is that the ground stop created travel disruptions and inconveniences for millions of people. And few are thrilled about that.

sports.title: Deion Sanders, Colorado score huge upset over No. 14 Houston
sports.summary: After the loss that dropped the Colorado Buffaloes to 3-6, coach Deion Sanders said, among other things, "The fans deserve better."
sports.body:
Colorado upset No. 14 Houston on Friday night in Boulder. The 42-32 victory moved the Buffaloes to 4-6.

Houston led 20-7 in the first half. Colorado had taken the lead by halftime, 21-20. Eventually, Colorado scored 28 straight points, taking a 35-20 lead.

For Houston, the loss killed any realistic hope of qualifying for the final 12-team College Football Playoff. For Colorado, the win keeps them alive for bowl eligibility — and possibly saves Sanders from having his fourth year in Colorado be his last.

Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports that the Saints sent Tyson on two separate visits to the University of Wisconsin to be evaluated by Dr. Heiderscheit and his team.

Hamstring injuries have been a major problem for Tyson, who was out for three months with a hamstring injury before finally making his NFL debut last week. Tyson also missed time at Arizona State last year because of a hamstring injury, and he didn’t run at either Arizona State’s Pro Day or the NFL Scouting Combine because of his hamstring.

But there’s hope for Tyson after his evaluations in Wisconsin. Heiderscheit was able to identify a weakness with Tyson’s hamstring that he thinks can be strengthened with a specific workout regimen that Tyson has been following.

Heiderscheit previously worked with Packers wide receiver Christian Watson and helped him recover from hamstring injuries, and it worked: Watson has started every game this season and in nine games already has career-highs with 49 catches for 879 yards, and he’s leading the NFL with an average of 17.9 yards per catch.

That’s the kind of player the Saints think Tyson can be, if he can stay healthy. Heiderscheit’s treatment may be the key to Tyson staying healthy.

sports.title: Joe Burrow can join Peyton Manning as only QBs with 4 total TDs in 5 straight games
sports.summary: A big game from Burrow on Sunday night would put him in some very exclusive company in NFL history.
sports.body:
Burrow has had at least four touchdowns, combined rushing and passing, in each of the last four games. If Burrow has another four-touchdown game on Sunday night, he will join Peyton Manning as the only quarterbacks in NFL history with at least four combined passing and rushing touchdowns in five consecutive games.

Burrow’s last four games: Three touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 34-17 win over the Falcons. Five touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 43-36 win over the Titans. Four touchdown passes in a 35-13 win over the Ravens. Four touchdown passes in a 31-24 win over the Dolphins.

Manning became the first quarterback to have five straight games with four touchdowns in Weeks 8-12 of 2004 with the Colts, when he had a six-touchdown game, two five-touchdown games and two four-touchdown games. (All of Manning’s touchdowns were passing, not rushing.) Manning was named NFL MVP that season.

And Burrow is an MVP candidate with the way he’s playing now. A win over the Steelers on Sunday night would put the Bengals in first place in the AFC North, and a big game with those big stakes would give a big boost to Burrow’s MVP chances.

sports.title: At least 50 different quarterbacks will have started games through Week 10
sports.summary: Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza will make his first career start on Sunday.
sports.body:
Via NBC Sports research, they’ll become the 48th, 49th, and 50th different quarterbacks to start games during the 2026 season.

It will be only the second time in the last 15 years (excluding the 1987 strike season) during which 50 different quarterbacks have started games in the first 10 weeks of a season.

If, for some reason, another quarterback makes his first start of the season on Sunday (that’s unlikely with Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock not having an injury designation for Sunday), it will be the second-most starters through 10 weeks since 1950.

In 1999, 55 different quarterbacks started games through the first 10 weeks of the season.

Most of the changes have arisen from injury. For the Raiders, the transition to Mendoza happened after Kirk Cousins was traded to the Vikings.

sports.title: FAA lifts ground stop, clearing the way for NFL teams to travel on Saturday
sports.summary: Eleven teams will be flying for Sunday games.
sports.body:
Friday’s sudden, and objectively concerning, decision by the FAA to issue only the second nationwide order to keep all planes from flying since 9/11 has ended.

The situation should result in no impact on NFL teams traveling to their road games for Sunday. It also should allow college teams to get to wherever they need to go for Saturday.

If it had happened one day later, the end result could have created chaos for NFL teams, significantly delaying their travel and turning their schedules for the night before the game upside down.

The situation came as a surprise to some NFL teams. For example, 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan learned about it during his Friday press conference.

Asked about the ground stop impacting the team’s plans for travel to Dallas on Saturday based on the ground stop, Shanahan said, “When did they do that?”

Eventually, Shanahan said, “I didn’t know. I just first heard.”

The 49ers plan to leave San Francisco at 1:00 p.m. PT on Saturday. Ten other teams will be traveling on Saturday, too.

sports.title: Victims claim Rex Ryan "almost killed" them with truck in Nasvhille
sports.summary: The victims in last week's Nashville incident involving former NFL coach Rex Ryan have come forward.
sports.body:
Via the California Post , attorney Michael Holland said that Ryan “ almost killed ” Holland and his wife with Ryan’s pickup truck, as they crossed the street.

“If we had been six inches further out,” Holland said, “I’d be in a hospital right now and so would my wife.”

Added Holland regarding Ryan: “He decided he wanted to turn and didn’t care, and just ran over both of my feet, my wife’s foot and got her leg too.”

Holland contends that Ryan didn’t stop, and that Holland caught up with the truck and pounded on the window.

“He was told in no uncertain terms what he had done, and instead of staying at the scene or even saying, ‘Sorry,’ he just got back in his vehicle and took off,” Holland said.

“I mean, just another inch or two, and his mirror or bumper would have taken off [my wife’s] knee,” Holland said. “His tire literally was like so close to her that it scraped her leg and ran over her feet and both of my feet. You just can’t do that. . . . My wife has already lost one of her toenails; I’m probably going to lose a couple of mine. Her leg is kind of scraped up . . . it hurt.”

Holland took a photo of Ryan’s red Ford Truck, with a Jets license plate holder and a vanity tag that says “HIT QBS.”

It’s entirely on brand for Ryan. Really, everything about the situation is.

sports.title: John Harbaugh: Cam Skattebo was not supposed to push on Jameis Winston sneak
sports.summary: Giants coach John Harbaugh defended running back Cam Skattebo, who stayed in his stance on a crucial Jameis Winston quarterback sneak during Thursday night's loss to the Commanders.
sports.body:
Harbaugh said the call was a quarterback sneak but not a tush push, and Skattebo wasn’t supposed to be pushing Winston.

“We had a certain check involved in it, so he wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing . We didn’t call the same [QB sneak] that we’ve been calling,” Harbaugh said, via Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News . “What else am I supposed to say? He wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing.”

Why the Giants wouldn’t want Skattebo to push Winston in an attempt to get the first down yardage is unclear, but the play looked strange, and it was a big one for the Giants, who had a 21-17 lead late in the fourth quarter at the time, but couldn’t hold the lead after getting stuffed on that quarterback sneak and lost 24-21.

sports.title: Nationwide ground stop potentially complicates NFL, college games
sports.summary: Some teams could get to game locations by ground. Many would have a hard time.
sports.body:
It’s only the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11. It’s apparently due to a widespread outage impacting air-traffic control functions.

Visiting NFL teams typically travel to the sites of their games on Saturday; if the situation lingers, some teams may not be able to get to where they need to be. More immediately, college teams that travel on Friday have a mess.

As noted by Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area, the 49ers usually travel on Friday for games that are at least two time zones away. For Sunday’s game against the Cowboys, they plan to travel on Saturday .

Some teams can get to the locations of their games by car or train. The distance from Minneapolis to Green Bay is 279 miles. For Buffalo to New Jersey (for Bills-Jets), it’s also less than 300 miles.

It’s roughly 290 miles fom Pittsburgh to Cincinnati, and 373 miles from L.A. to Phoenix.

For the other games (particularly Chargers-Ravens on Monday night), it’s a long way to go via ground transportation.

sports.title: Report: Eagles to release veteran OL Fred Johnson
sports.summary: The Eagles are releasing veteran offensive tackle Fred Johnson, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports.
sports.body:
The move comes shortly after veteran receiver Hollywood Brown requested his release , and the sides reached a non-injury settlement.

The Eagles have seen an overhaul of their offensive line this season.

Johnson was serving as a backup to rookie Markel Bell at right tackle since the in-season retirement of Lane Johnson. He saw action in seven games this season, playing 24 offensive snaps and 22 on special teams.

Johnson, 29, returned on a one-year contract this offseason.

He originally joined the Eagles in 2023, playing 58 games with 14 starts.

sports.title: Eagles will release WR Hollywood Brown, at his request
sports.summary: Say goodbye to Philadelphia.
sports.body:
Receiver Hollywood Brown, who was available in trade but had no takers, will now be released at his request , via Tim McManus of ESPN.

Thanks to a “noninjury settlement” (which presumably includes Brown waiving his right to termination pay), Brown will be released. Because the trade deadline has passed, Brown’s contract will be subject to waivers.

Brown signed a one-year deal with a $3.7 million signing bonus and a $1.3 million base salary. In addition to waiving his right to termination pay, Brown possibly agreed to return a portion of the bonus money.

A first-round pick of the Ravens in 2019, Brown appeared in only four games for the Eagles, with one start. He caught five passes for 63 yards.

Brown spent three years with the Ravens. In 2022, he was traded to the Cardinals. After two seasons in Arizona, he spent 2024 and 2025 with the Chiefs.

The minimum base salary could prompt another team to make a waivers claim — especially if that team would be willing to pay more than the prorated minimum to add him to the roster for the rest of the season.

Brown’s best year came in 2021, with 91 catches for 1,008 yards and six touchdowns.

sports.title: Robert Saleh says he and Liam Coen are good after "misunderstanding" last year
sports.summary: When the Titans face the Jaguars on Sunday, Robert Saleh and Liam Coen will coach against each other for the first time since their run-in last year, when they exchanged words on the field over something Saleh, then the defensive coordinator of the 49ers, said something about Coen that Coen didn't a
sports.body:
Last year, Saleh said that Coen’s team was good at stealing signals, intending it as a compliment for how good they are at recognizing what the opposing defense was doing. Coen interpreted it as an accusation of cheating and confronted Saleh on the field after the game.

Today Saleh was asked about that, and he said he and Coen have spoken and there are no hard feelings.

“Liam’s great, man,” Saleh said. “We’ve had plenty of interactions. The whole thing is what it was, a little misunderstanding, poor words on my part. But they’re doing a great job. I love what they’re doing offensively. They’ve definitely got an identity. And then [defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile] on the other side. Overall as an organization, they’ve done a really nice job.”

Coen’s confrontational approach toward Saleh after the game last year seemed like an overreaction, but no one can dispute that Coen has done a great job building the Jaguars. Saleh knows he’s going up against a good coach on Sunday, and he won’t provide any bulletin-board material.

sports.title: Kenneth Walker did not practice Friday with groin tightness

Head coach Andy Reid told reporters in his Friday press conference that running back Kenneth Walker sat out Friday’s practice after reporting tightness in his groin.

“We’ll just see how he feels through this afternoon with rehab and through tomorrow,” Reid said. “Somewhere he tweaked it. So, we’ll see. ... He was tight this morning.”

While Reid did not explicitly say a game status, it sounds as if Walker will be questionable.

“We’re kind of feeling it out just to see where we’re at with that thing,” Reid said. “We’re not going to put him at risk or anything like that — that’s not how we roll. So, if he can go, he can go. If he can’t, he can’t.”

Walker leads the league averaging 109.0 rushing yards per game. He’s tallied a total of 872 yards with seven rushing touchdowns in eight games. He’s also caught 26 passes for 172 yards with four TDs.

If Walker is not able to play, rookie Emmett Johnson would be in line to start and carry the load.

“Yeah, if Emmett has to do it, then we all have [confidence],” Reid said. “He’s going to play anyway, whether Ken’s there or not there, he’s gonna play. But everybody has confidence in him, yeah.”

Johnson has 111 rushing yards on 26 carries with a touchdown and 14 receptions for 237 yards with a TD so far this year.

sports.body: The Jets recently signed former Colts offensive lineman Blake Freeland to their active roster from the Bengals’ practice squad. Today, we break him down in detail. The 25-year old Freeland is listed at 6’7” and 302 pounds and was a fourth round pick out of BYU in 2023. He has started nine games in his career, all of which were for the Colts in his rookie year. Background Freeland was a three-star high school recruit but headed to BYU with zero experience of playing on the offensive line having been a quarterback for two years before moving to tight end and defensive end as a senior. He also played basketball and represented his school in shot put and javelin throwing. On his arrival at BYU, Freeland converted to offensive tackle but didn’t see the field until the middle of his freshman season. However, he ended up starting the last seven games and held up reasonably well, as he only allowed one sack. He didn’t begin his sophomore year as a starter, but ended up making a total of eight starts in 2020, during which he showed promise by not allowing a sack all year. In 2021 and 2022, Freeland started all 26 games and was twice named to Phil Steele’s all-Independent Conference first team. He was also a third team AP all-American in 2022. Heading into the 2023 pre-draft process, Freeland was being touted as a possible day two pick. However, his rawness was exposed during Senior Bowl week. Even so, he managed to stablize his stock with good workouts at the combine and his pro day. The Colts eventually drafted Freeland in the fourth round and he started off his rookie year on the bench. He soon made his first start due to a week four injury, and by the end of the year had started nine games. In 2024, he failed to earn a starting role and spent the first half of the season as a healthy scratch. He played in the last eight games, although he only played 23 offensive snaps, 22 of which were in the season finale. In year three, a serious leg injury during preseason forced Freeland to spend the entire year on injured reserve and then he faced an uphill battle to make the team out of training camp this summer. After being released in final cuts following preseason, Freeland signed to Cincinnati’s practice squad before being poached by the Jets last month following Max Mitchell’s concussion.
