sports.body: The Buffalo Bills and New York Jets face off this weekend, and their seasons couldn’t be going in more opposite directions. Buffalo has won four straight games, and they are 7-1 overall for the season. The Jets, meanwhile, have lost four straight games, and they sit at just 2-7 overall. Where both teams are equal, though, is in the win column vs. other AFC East foes. The Jets have dropped games to both the New England Patriots and Miami Dolphins this season, while the Bills had their only loss come at the hands of those Patriots. Neither Buffalo nor New York has a division win this season, something that both teams want to change on Sunday. How can the Bills overcome the Jets? Well, they’ll have to start by taking care of their own business, but they’ll also need to keep tabs on the Jets’ top players. Here are five Jets to watch this week against Buffalo. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Geno Smith The veteran has been solid in his second go-round with the Jets, as he’s thrown 12 touchdown passes against just three interceptions so far this season. Smith’s 100.5 quarterback rating is outstanding, as is his 67.5% completion rate on the year. However, he’s also taken a whopping 28 sacks for a league-leading 236 yards lost. If the Bills can win their matchups up front, Smith will hold the ball, and at 36 years old, he doesn’t have the mobility he once had. Smith was never a great runner, but he’s not someone I’d call elusive in the pocket. Buffalo should look to heat him up early in the game before giving him more simulated pressure looks as the game progresses. Speed up his clock to force him to make mistakes. He’ll hold the ball and take a sack over throwing an interception more often than not, so Buffalo’s defensive front needs to be ready to feast. RB Breece Hall The explosive runner has ten career 100-yard games on the ground, and two of those 100-yard games are against the Bills. Hall missed time this year with a quad injury, and he returned last week for the Jets’ 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. He carried 15 times for 61 yards in the game, which was his second-best output of the season. sports.body: Look at that. Former New York Jets defensive back Jim Leonhard is the defensive coordinator for the Buffalo Bills. Leonhard played for the Jets from 2009 through 2011. Ah yes, the glory days. The Jets went to back-to-back AFC Championship games and it felt like the team was on top of the football world. Looking back on that era and living through those moments reminds me of the line from Andy Bernard in “The Office”: “I wish there was a way to know you’re in the good old days, before you’ve actually left them.” Jets fans thought we’d be riding that wave forever, and then suddenly, out of nowhere, it was over. Leonhard was asked about his many connections to the Jets organization during his media availability ahead of Week 10. Here’s a did-you-know segment: Leonhard played against Geno Smith as a player in the NFL. During Leonhard’s final year playing in the NFL in 2014, he played under first-year coach Aaron Glenn with the Cleveland Browns. Leonhard has known Jets running back Braelon Allen since he was 16 years old. Before making the jump to the NFL coaching world, Leonhard was in the college ranks at Wisconsin and got to recruit Allen as a high schooler. sports.body: Yuck. The New York Giants might be 5-2-1, but they’re leading what many see as among the worst divisions in the NFL. Tonight, they take on the 2-5-1 Washington Commanders — that’s right, a team they played to a tie earlier this season. Will there be similar “fireworks” for Thursday Night Football? It would be great if this game was exciting — and even better if it wasn’t in primetime. It’s safe to say that football fans have had their fill of these teams, of the NFC East, and the NFC in general. At least Week 10 gives us two AFC showdowns. The trouble is that the one on Monday night is about as bad as it gets. There aren’t any rooting interests here as it relates to the Buffalo Bills. You might find yourself cheering for the Commanders just to hand the Giants a loss, or at least see them make good on their horrible decisions that led to the tie in the previous matchup. Depending on how far back your Bills fandom goes, you may find it impossible rooting for an NFC East team (except when they face the New England Patriots, and probably the Kansas City Chiefs). There’s a lot of bad football being trotted out to the masses this season. but this is what you get tonight and you’re probably watching until the end. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 10 of Thursday Night Football. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!
